title: migrate: GBL-* migrations apply after 1xxx due to lexicographic sort — fresh-DB bootstrap fails on 1135
notes: zig build migrate fails against a fresh/empty database with C42703 'column "tenant_type" of relation "tenant" does not exist' on 1135_iss0114_backfill_public_tenant_storage_mode.sql. Existing developer databases are unaffected because they applied GBL-119_env01_tenant_type_field.sql while it was still named 080_env01_tenant_type_field.sql (the original name is still in that file's header comment). Reproduces 100% on any new database: new workspace, CI, or a new contributor's first setup. Discovered while provisioning the second parallel workspace at c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\2\R-Co.
root_cause: src/db/migrations.zig sorts pending migrations with a raw lexicographic std.mem.lessThan on filename (~line 185). Its comment claims 'zero-padded NNN_ prefix ensures numeric order', which stopped holding when GBL- prefixed migrations were added: '1' (0x31) < 'G' (0x47), so every GBL-* file applies after every 1xxx_* file. The same module already defines migrationOrder(), which encodes the intended ordering (strip 'GBL-', add 1000 offset => GBL-119 -> 1119, correctly before 1135), but it is used only for the out-of-order detection check, never for the apply sort. The two disagree and the sort wins. Systemic, not a single bad file: GBL-112..GBL-133 map to 1112..1133 and should interleave among the 11xx numeric migrations.
candidate_resolution: Sort by migrationOrder(filename) with filename as a deterministic tiebreak for equal orders, so the apply order matches the order the out-of-order check already enforces. Correct the stale sort comment. Add regression coverage asserting GBL-119 sorts before 1135.
acceptance_criteria: src/db/migrations.zig orders pending migrations by migrationOrder() with a deterministic tiebreak
zig build migrate exits 0 against a completely empty database
zig build migrate is a no-op (exits 0) on an already-migrated database
regression test asserts GBL-119 sorts before 1135

resolution.summary:
Made migrationOrder() the single ordering authority for migration application, in BOTH runners. The apply sort previously used a raw lexicographic std.mem.lessThan on the filename while migrationOrder() (already used by the out-of-order detection check) encoded the intended order; the two disagreed and the sort governed execution. Both sorts now order by migrationOrder() with the filename as a deterministic tiebreak for equal orders.

IMPORTANT: the bug existed in TWO places. src/db/migrations.zig (runForSchema, used by the server and test harness) was the file named in the diagnosis, but `zig build migrate` actually executes a duplicated copy of the same logic in src/tools/migrate.zig. Fixing only the former left the reported symptom completely unchanged; both had to be fixed.

Out-of-order detection was also reworked so the fix does not brick pre-existing databases. Previously the check compared each pending file against a global max-applied watermark. Because the old wrong sort applied every GBL-* file after every 1xxx_* file, existing databases legitimately carry a backlog of pending GBL files (orders 1112..1133) sitting below an already-applied 1134/1135 — judging that backlog against the global watermark would have returned OutOfOrderMigration and permanently bricked every existing environment. The check is now scoped to inversions encountered within the current pass: walking past an applied file advances a 'walked_order' watermark, so an applied migration only constrains files that sort AFTER it. The legacy backlog is grandfathered in and applied, while a genuinely misnumbered new migration is still rejected. The now-dead max_applied/max_applied_order variables were removed rather than left in place, since leaving two disagreeing notions of 'order' is the exact defect this issue fixed.
resolution.verification:
All commands run in workspace 2 against the r-co-2 docker stack.

REPRODUCTION (pre-fix): `zig build migrate` against the empty bpm_test DB (localhost:5453) failed with C42703 'column "tenant_type" of relation "tenant" does not exist' on 1135_iss0114_backfill_public_tenant_storage_mode.sql — exactly as reported.

(a) FROM-EMPTY: created scratch DB fresh_check on localhost:5452. Post-fix the apply order is correct — recorded applied order is 1111 -> GBL-112..GBL-119 -> 1134 -> 1135, i.e. GBL-119 now correctly precedes 1135. The ordering defect itself is fully resolved. However `zig build migrate` still exits 1 on a fresh DB due to a SEPARATE, independent circular dependency filed as ISS-0604 / GH #470 (public-only migration 1135 executes in the per-tenant pass, which skips GBL files, so it cannot see GBL-119's column; the resulting unready tenant then trips GBL-116's TNT-07 pre-flight). Proof the cycle is the ONLY remaining blocker: applying GBL-119 by hand to public and re-running migrate drove the DB to 106/106 public migrations applied with exit 0.

(b) RE-RUN NO-OP: on that fully-migrated fresh_check DB, `zig build migrate` reported 'No new migrations to apply.' and exited 0. Verified twice.

(c) EXISTING ENVIRONMENT: bpm_dev (localhost:5452) is itself a real pre-existing victim of this bug — 83 public migrations applied through 1134, zero GBL-* applied. This is precisely the state that would trip a global-watermark out-of-order check. Post-fix migrate produced NO 'Out-of-order migration' error and successfully applied GBL-112..GBL-115 (orders 1112..1115) even though 1134 was already applied — going 83 -> 87 public migrations. This directly demonstrates the grandfathering works and existing environments are not bricked. bpm_dev then stops at the independent ISS-0604 cycle, same as a fresh DB.

(d) BUILD: `zig build` exits 0. `zig build 2>&1 | grep -i 'error set'` produces no output.

(e) TESTS: `zig build test` exits 0 (full suite). `.venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/lint_sql_param_types.py src tests` reports 0 BLOCKER / 0 MAJOR / 0 MINOR.

REGRESSION COVERAGE: 4 new tests in tests/unit/db_test.zig (TC-DB-01-06) assert GBL-119 sorts before 1135, that migrationOrder() maps the GBL- prefix into the 1xxx band, that a mixed GBL/numeric set sorts into correct interleaved order, and that equal-order files use the filename tiebreak. These were MUTATION-TESTED: temporarily reverting the comparator to the old raw lexicographic form made 2 of them fail with the expected diagnostics, confirming they are genuine regression guards rather than restatements of default behaviour. Restored and re-verified passing.

Both scratch databases (fresh_check, legacy_check) were dropped after verification.
resolution.prevention: The root hazard was two copies of the ordering rule that were allowed to disagree — first the sort vs migrationOrder() within src/db/migrations.zig, and second the entire duplicated runner in src/tools/migrate.zig. migrationOrder() in src/db/migrations.zig is now `pub` and documented as the single ordering authority, and the duplicate in src/tools/migrate.zig carries an explicit 'MUST stay identical / if you change one, change both' warning. The unit tests pin the ordering contract so future drift fails the build rather than silently corrupting bootstrap order.
